title: Critical potassium
text: Potassium at or above 6.5 mmol/L, or at or below 2.5 mmol/L, is a critical value. It must be communicated to the responsible clinician at once and confirmed by read-back.

title: Critical glucose
text: Glucose at or above 27.8 mmol/L (500 mg/dL), or at or below 2.2 mmol/L (40 mg/dL), is a critical value and must be communicated at once with read-back.

title: Critical hemoglobin
text: Hemoglobin at or below 7.0 g/dL, or at or above 20.0 g/dL, is a critical value and must be communicated at once with read-back.

title: Critical sodium
text: Sodium at or below 120 mmol/L, or at or above 160 mmol/L, is a critical value and must be communicated at once with read-back.

title: Time to communicate
text: A critical value is communicated to the responsible clinician within minutes. The time, the person told and the value repeated back are recorded.

title: Hemolyzed sample
text: A hemolyzed sample can falsely raise potassium. When the hemolysis index is high, advise a new sample and tell the clinician that the result may be unreliable.

title: Communicate anyway
text: A critical potassium with a high hemolysis index is still communicated at once. The recollect advice is added to the communication; it never replaces it.

title: Sample quality indices
text: Sample quality indices for hemolysis, lipemia and icterus above the laboratory limit make a result doubtful. A hemolysis index above 100 is high.

title: New sample after communication
text: After a critical result has been communicated, a new sample may be requested to confirm it when the sample quality was doubtful.

title: Acute drop of hemoglobin
text: An acute drop of hemoglobin of more than 3 g/dL within 24 hours must be raised to critical even when the new value is inside the critical limit.

title: Dialysis patient
text: A patient on scheduled dialysis can have a stable high potassium for days. A value close to the earlier results of the same patient is explained by the context, but a value above the critical limit still needs read-back.

title: Earlier results
text: Compare the result with the earlier results of the same patient for the same analyte in the last seven days. A large change is more important than the absolute value.

title: Age groups
text: Critical limits depend on the age group: neonate under one year, child from one to seventeen years, adult from eighteen years.

title: Falling glucose
text: A glucose result near the low critical limit in a patient with a falling trend needs attention before it reaches the limit.

title: Reference unit
text: Each analyte is judged in its reference unit. Results in another unit are converted to the reference unit before the critical limits are applied.

title: Unit that cannot be converted
text: A result whose unit cannot be converted is not released. It goes to a person unless the value is critical in any known unit.

title: Ambiguous result
text: When the value is near the critical limit and the sample quality or the earlier results disagree, the case goes to a person to decide.

title: Low confidence
text: An answer given with low confidence is never used to release a result. It goes to a person.

title: The agent never lowers
text: The agent can raise the severity of a result above the rule floor and can never lower it. A result critical by rule stays critical.

title: Read-back
text: A critical result is closed only after the person who communicated it repeats the value back and it matches the original value.
